German lexical decision by L1 and L2 speakers

Source: R/data.R
lexical_decision_l2.Rd

30 participants (15 L1 and 15 L2 speakers of German) each respond to the same 40 German words. L2 speakers are slower and more sensitive to frequency.

Usage

lexical_decision_l2

Format

A tibble with 1200 rows and 6 columns:

participant

Participant ID, P01 to P30.

group

"L1" or "L2".

word

Word ID, w01 to w40.

log_freq

log10 word frequency, 1 to 6.

length

Length in letters, 3 to 13; frequent words are shorter.

rt

Reaction time in ms.

Source

data-raw/lexical_decision_l2.R

Details

True model:

log(rt) = 6.55 + 0.16 * L2 + p0 + w0 + slope * (log_freq - 3.5)
  + 0.017 * (length - 7) + e
slope = -0.035 - 0.03 * L2 + p1

By-participant intercepts p0 have SD 0.085 and slopes p1 SD 0.015; by-word intercepts w0 have SD 0.04; residual SD 0.09.

Examples

lexical_decision_l2$freq_c <- lexical_decision_l2$log_freq - 3.5
lexical_decision_l2$length_c <- lexical_decision_l2$length - 7
if (requireNamespace("lme4", quietly = TRUE)) {
  m <- lme4::lmer(log(rt) ~ group * freq_c + length_c + (1 + freq_c | participant) +
                    (1 | word), data = lexical_decision_l2)
  lme4::fixef(m)
}
#>    (Intercept)        groupL2         freq_c       length_c groupL2:freq_c 
#>     6.53334179     0.20409400    -0.02452505     0.01448920    -0.04226105
